Where should the OP-01 stream spike land? BK-506 reserves sdd/research/bk-506-faithfulness-trial/ for its pre-registered trial, and RFC-0029 R4 keeps record-derived oracle work away from it.

options.label: bk-485-op01-stream-spike/ (Recommended)
options.description: sdd/research/bk-485-op01-stream-spike/ with README + repo-only report.md, under BK-485 (step 5's model and 0.33 comparison). The report states that it is not BK-506's trial and must not feed it.

options.label: Under BK-505 instead
options.description: File it as record-quality evidence (one extraction of OP-01, stale-filter finding). Fits the extraction half; the conformance half fits BK-505 less well.

questions.question: Rule RF4 assumes a cancellation is ignored when a read needs no transfer, which O45 reads as contradicting D20 ('a cancelled stream read ... is then Closed', in every state). Fix it before landing?

options.label: Fix RF4, rerun, then land (Recommended)
options.description: Make cancellation close the stream in every state per D20, rerun all four SUTs, and record the before/after. The committed oracle then matches the record as the audit reads it.

options.label: Land as run, note it
options.description: Freeze the spike exactly as it ran, and record RF4's conflict with D20 as a known defect in the report.

questions.question: What should ship alongside the spike folder?

options.label: Trace + BK-485 dossier line (Recommended)
options.description: sdd/traces/bk-485-op01-stream-spike.yml (precedent: bk-484-key-model-research.yml), plus one line in BK-485's dossier pointing to the spike. No backlog items, no CHANGELOG (contributor-process only).

options.label: Trace only
options.description: Ship the trace and leave BK-485's dossier and body untouched; the spike is discoverable only through sdd/research/ and the trace.

options.label: Folder only
options.description: No trace and no dossier line. Lightest, but breaks the precedent that research on a backlog item ships its trace.

options.label: Include with caveat (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the script and its output as step 1, with the report stating the filter is stale and that the Axis status table is the current source. That is itself a BK-505 data point.

options.label: Drop it
options.description: Land only the stream slice (rules, model, conformance). The stale-filter observation survives as one line in the report.

questions.question: Where should the classification live?

Spec kind for a failure response triggered by the environment (e.g. 'an Open stream meets E8 → the category is raised, Failed'): SPEC-DESIGN Rule 2 says a witness needing a behaviour outside the library's control is 'environment'. Which kind?

options.label: Lifetime, trigger apart (Recommended)
options.description: The clause states the library's response, which a test checks by injecting E8; the trigger facet already records the World row. 'Environment' stays for what the library relies on (assumptions, D43 deviations). Matches the pilot (32 lifetime, 1 environment).

options.label: Environment
options.description: Read Rule 2 literally: any clause whose witness needs a World event is environment. Moves every storage-failure and cancellation clause there, so 'lifetime' only holds fault-free behaviour.

options.label: Raise it with Rule 2
options.description: Classify as lifetime for now and file the ambiguity against SPEC-DESIGN Rule 2 for its owner to settle; the classification follows the answer.

questions.question: Trigger for storage failures: the pilot used E8 for 'any failure the library cannot mend'. For the whole record?

options.label: World rows as a set (Recommended)
options.description: trigger lists every Environment row that can cause the clause (e.g. [E7, E8, E10, E12]), taken from D19's exposure table and D34/D96; precise, and checkable against the Environment.

options.label: Category instead
options.description: trigger names the D34 category (unavailable, timeout, changed, ...) and leaves the rows to D34; fewer values, but two places to read.

options.label: Keep one row
options.description: As the pilot: one representative row. Cheapest; loses which rows reach which clause.

questions.question: State facet: the pilot mixes single states and sets (not-Closed, any). For the whole record?

options.label: Sets allowed (Recommended)
options.description: Keep named sets (not-Closed, any) where the behaviour is the same in each; a clause per state only where outcomes differ. The check expands a set when comparing with the rules.

options.label: One state per clause
options.description: Split every set into single states. Each clause maps to one state-table cell, at about 2–3× the clauses with repeated text.

options.label: Whole record, then route (Recommended)
options.description: Classify all 156 decisions (whole reads, text, concurrency, profiles), then route the not-decided behaviours under RFC-0030 C1 and file Local's gaps (C1–C8) as backlog items with the classification's IDs.

options.label: File Local gaps first
options.description: File C1–C8 now (C8 is a silent truncation in 0.33's Local), then the whole-record pass and the routing.

options.label: Open PRs first
options.description: Open the two PRs (rerun addendum, BK-511 pilot) for review before more work stacks on them.

questions.question: After the facet decisions, what runs next?

Three of four classification groups hit a strict decode failure (text form) and filed it under 'caller-error', which is wrong: the caller did nothing invalid, the content can't be decoded. How should the path facet handle it?

options.label: New path: content-failure (Recommended)
options.description: Add 'content-failure' for decode errors (and any content the item holds but the call can't use). Clean split from caller errors; ~5 clauses move.

options.label: Under storage-failure
options.description: No new value; treat a decode failure as one more failure the library can't mend. Mixes World faults with content faults in that path's counts.

options.label: Keep caller-error
options.description: Leave as is, on the reading that the caller chose the encoding. Keeps the vocabulary small but miscounts caller errors.

questions.question: 11 error-category clauses (X01–X04, X06–X08, X12, X13, X16, X22) are marked 'partly' because open item O9 blocks every failure-category clause (D108) and D27 calls the category names working names. The behaviour itself is decided. How to mark them?

options.label: Decided, gap O9 (Recommended)
options.description: Behaviour counts as decided; gap = OP-01/O9 keeps the naming/landing block visible. Status then measures behaviour, not landing readiness.

options.label: Keep partly
options.description: Status also reflects whether the clause can land. 'Not decided' list stays at 19 and is dominated by O9.

questions.question: Cancellation appears with trigger 'Runtime' (actor) in the pilot and groups, though Environment row E14 describes exactly that event. Which should the trigger facet carry?

options.label: E14 (Recommended)
options.description: Triggers then always name an Environment row when one exists, matching the 'World rows as a set' decision; Runtime stays only for events no row names.

options.label: Runtime
options.description: Keep the actor name as the pilot did; E14 never appears as a trigger.

questions.question: Clauses covering both a whole read and a stream's open got state 'open-call', 'any' or 'none' inconsistently. How should state read for a call that creates no stream yet?

options.label: 'none' for both (Recommended)
options.description: State is a stream state; a whole read and an open both act before a stream exists, so 'none'. Drop 'open-call' (pilot S01, S02 become 'none').

options.label: Keep 'open-call'
options.description: 'open-call' for anything that includes an open, 'none' for whole-only. Keeps the open distinguishable in the state view.

options.description: Add 'content-failure' for decode errors (and any content the item holds but the call can't use). Clean split from caller errors; ~5 clauses move.

options.description: Leave as is, on the reading that the caller chose the encoding. Keeps the vocabulary small but miscounts caller errors.

options.description: Behaviour counts as decided; gap = OP-01/O9 keeps the naming/landing block visible. Status then measures behaviour, not landing readiness.

questions.question: 11 error-category clauses (X01–X04, X06–X08, X12, X13, X16, X22) are marked 'partly' because open item O9 blocks every failure-category clause (D108) and D27 calls the category names working names. The behaviour itself is decided. How to mark them?

options.description: Triggers then always name an Environment row when one exists, matching the 'World rows as a set' decision; Runtime stays only for events no row names.

options.description: Keep the actor name as the pilot did; E14 never appears as a trigger.
